chunks.about-about#0:
Software engineer working on AI agents, retrieval systems and reproducible evaluation. Currently pursuing an M.Tech. in Software Engineering at the National University of Singapore. I build systems that turn model outputs into controlled, executable actions, then measure how well they work.

I studied Computer Science at KAIST before joining NUS. My experience spans enterprise agents, industrial computer vision and Java Web development.

My independent projects explore coding agents built from first principles, multi-path retrieval and context management. Controlled experiments, including negative results, guide the design.
chunks.about-about#1: From Java Web development to industrial vision and enterprise agents, my focus has remained on execution boundaries, real-world performance and reproducible evidence.

chunks.about-experience#0:
Delivered four agents for engineering, product planning and project management teams in Shanghai, serving around 500 internal users in total.

Built agents for connector selection, competitive analysis, PRD generation and review, and black-box testing, addressing cost-reduction briefs from three departments.

Connector selection: an 8.5k-line Python system using Flask, LangChain and MongoDB. An LLM decomposes requests into exact, fuzzy and range queries across five product collections with automatic field mapping. Engineer-confirmed results become reusable knowledge-base templates. Shipped eight releases, including a dataset migration and a simpler fallback path.
chunks.about-experience#1:
Competitive analysis: an LLM-driven crawler collects public vehicle-owner reviews into MongoDB. Six chapter-level agents form a pipeline that produces a structured, evidence-backed report.

AUT: a 3.1k-line Python black-box testing tool. Playwright locates the chat interface, captures live API calls and produces replayable request templates, with manual handoff for CAPTCHA, SSO and MFA. Staged load tests stop on success-rate, error-rate and p95 thresholds; probes check prompt injection, cross-session leakage and output stability.
chunks.about-experience#2: Measured the connector agent at 100% success and 14.2-second p95 with 20 concurrent users. At 500 concurrent users, success fell to 94.9%, with 51 of 1,000 responses empty or malformed. These measurements identify a degradation point, not a universal performance guarantee.
chunks.about-experience#3:
Built vision algorithms for a special-operations competency examination system in Zhengzhou, owning deployment across three production lines.

Worked on an examination system with the municipal emergency-management bureau. Four to five synchronized cameras assess procedural compliance and completeness. The system ran live exams every working day for over a month; I owned three production lines and defined annotation standards with the data team.

Replaced YOLO detection plus hand-written rules with graph-based scoring. YOLOv8 extracts component centres, sizes, angles and classes; assembly constraints connect them into a graph, and a graph convolutional network predicts installation and step-completion states.
chunks.about-experience#4: Models reached around 90% accuracy in internal acceptance testing. Human co-invigilation and tablet scoring provided a fallback so an algorithm failure would not interrupt an exam.
chunks.about-experience#5:
Worked on intelligent systems and automation in January and February 2024.

Helped develop an interactive periodic-table display, connecting the visual interface, control logic and physical actuators for an educational installation.

Integrated physical exhibits with digital controls to present chemistry and safety concepts, supporting changes in display state and visitor interaction.

Taught introductory robotic-arm programming to visiting students and guided the assembly, debugging and verification of racing kits.

Independently modelled, printed and iterated FDM prototypes for the display and its structural parts. Used Yamaha robot teach programming and I/O control in basic equipment commissioning.
chunks.about-experience#6:
Developed and maintained enterprise Java Web features and tuned database access under peak traffic.

Built business features, accompanying front-end pages and a WeChat Mini Program within an existing enterprise system.

Re-sized the connection pool, replaced row-by-row reads and writes with batches, and simplified queries. Peak-hour connection-wait alarms stopped after the changes.

The lasting lesson was methodological: locate where the waiting actually happens before changing a parameter.
chunks.about-projects#0:
A decision-support agent that turns supplier quotes into comparable evidence. Code produces a reference ranking, the agent makes a recommendation using read-only tools, and a buyer approves or overrides it.

A four-person team project for the NUS-ISS “Show Me Your Agent” hackathon, demonstrated with synthetic supplier data.

Normalizes price, lead time, payment terms, on-time delivery and quality; applies hard constraints before calculating reference scores and negotiation gaps.

Calls a model through an Ollama-compatible gateway and parses JSON tool requests. The agent may depart from the reference ranking when supported by tool evidence; structured output is validated.
chunks.about-projects#1:
Treats quote text as untrusted input, with injection detection, read-only tools, supplier eligibility checks, fallback behavior, and normal and adversarial evaluation cases.

Logs model recommendations, buyer approvals or override reasons, and request IDs. The system recommends; it never places orders.

An installable skill and plugin that asks coding assistants to explain mechanisms and use concrete examples. Evaluation checks that clearer wording preserves technical accuracy.

Ten writing rules target vague wording and unnecessary jargon while preserving precise terminology and an appropriate register for expert readers.

Provides a skill, Claude Code plugin configuration and an optional always-on hook for different assistant workflows.

Python scripts manage test cases and a scoring rubric, with reproducible shuffling and anonymization of responses for blind evaluation.

Provides continuous-integration checks and offline validation of test cases and scoring rules without model calls or credentials.

chunks.about-projects#4:
A self-assessment experiment about work tasks. It examines routine, knowledge, responsibility and physical presence to help people reflect on the division of work between humans and AI.

Uses 28 questions across four axes: task routine, knowledge codifiability, responsibility for consequences, and embodied presence. Their combinations produce 16 types.

Includes reverse-scored questions, with feedback loops and bargaining position recorded as additional labels rather than determinants of the type.

Built with native HTML, JavaScript and Canvas. The questionnaire, scoring and result-image generation run in the browser without a backend.

chunks.about-projects#6:
A command-line coding assistant built without an agent framework. Repository maps, sandbox escape tests and A/A controls put each design decision to the test.

A native tool-calling ReAct loop with seven tools. SEARCH/REPLACE editing uses a four-tier matching chain to handle whitespace and partial-line drift. Shell commands run inside macOS Seatbelt, with boundaries verified by escape tests: about 1,300 lines of core code and 52 tests, including nine escape tests.
chunks.about-projects#7:
The repository map uses tree-sitter definitions and references to build a file graph, then personalized PageRank to rank context for the task. Constraining edges by actual Python imports raised edge precision from 32% to 100% without dropping a true edge. IDF-weighted seeds addressed query understanding.

On a 112-file repository, the map reduced task steps by 21% and input tokens by 33%. These figures describe that controlled experiment, not a guarantee across repositories.
chunks.about-projects#8:
The evaluation harness runs an A/A arm by default, putting effects beside their noise floor; this led me to retract an earlier claim. In this architecture, output caps made history compression unnecessary. Sub-agent isolation used 42% more total tokens for 22% less main-loop context, without improving completion or correctness. Committed traces make the measurements reproducible.

chunks.about-projects#9:
Five retrieval paths, visible score breakdowns and repeatable experiments replace opaque weighting with a measurable ranking problem.

Runs filename and path, section title, SQLite FTS5, dense-vector and entity-graph retrieval in parallel. Four independent weighting strategies score the results, which merge per file with per-path scores exposed.

Moves hard-coded scoring parameters into hot-reloadable configuration. Files the model actually opens provide weak relevance labels, with provenance recorded so they are not mistaken for human annotations.
chunks.about-projects#10:
Optimizes NDCG rather than ratio-style metrics that can improve by collapsing weight onto a single path while the ranking worsens. Grid search maps the space; repeated independent genetic-algorithm runs separate gains from noise.

Index schemas, configuration and ranking metrics are covered by 17 tests. The pipeline runs offline without an API key.

chunks.about-projects#11:
Turns natural-language questions over uploaded spreadsheets into verified SQL, result tables and charts. Structured plans, whitelisted actions and role-based isolation define what the system can execute.

A FastAPI and SQLAlchemy backend spans 76 modules, 23,331 lines and 56 test files, using MySQL, Redis, MinIO and Qwen. A 7,487-line React 19 front end streams over SSE. Rolled out to 20+ internal pilot users, whose trial feedback estimated roughly two hours of manual work saved per person per day.
chunks.about-projects#12:
Refactored a fixed LLM workflow into a Planner–Executor design. The planner emits only a structured plan: intent, target fields, actions, constraints and failure policy. The executor runs whitelisted actions over read-only SQL with table, field and permission checks.

Persists session context, generated SQL and chart configuration so follow-up questions can refer to earlier turns. Data isolation follows organization and role boundaries.

chunks.about-research#0:
Rong He | 2026-10-01 | Preprint · Zenodo v1

How should a best-of-n deployment budget be chosen from a fixed candidate pool with limited correctness labels? This work gives matching minimax expected-regret bounds for adaptive and non-adaptive labelling. The extra logarithmic cost of non-adaptivity affects only the label term. The bounds account for pool size, label budget and menu width. Exact checks and synthetic diagnostics illustrate finite-budget limits; they do not establish gains on real tasks.

Zenodo: [10.5281/zenodo.23086434](https://zenodo.org/records/23086434)
chunks.about-research#1:
Rong He | 2026-09-28 | Preprint · Zenodo v1.0

Compares a finite menu of Boolean queries that return either a truth value at an unknown state or an exact population probability. For pointwise minimax error e and population minimax excess zero-one risk R, proves e ≤ R ≤ 2e. Equality is universally preserved when e = 0 or e ≥ 1/3; every attainable error between 0 and 1/3 admits an interface with R > e. The result concerns exact, restricted query interfaces, not model performance.

Zenodo: [10.5281/zenodo.23020314](https://zenodo.org/records/23020314)
chunks.about-research#2:
Rong He | 2026-09-15 | Preprint · arXiv v1

Studies what task decomposition buys and loses: smaller root context, but less of the information discovered by leaves surviving the journey back. Models retention as r(b) = 1/b, validates it on 20,000 irregular trees, and analyses 600 production deep-research traces and 743,819 tool calls. Flat structures are optimal for yield; decomposition earns its keep through context integrity and cost.

arXiv: [arXiv:2609.17464](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2609.17464)
chunks.about-research#3:
Rong He | 2026-09-12 | Preprint · arXiv v1

Recasts the ordering of reusable prompt chunks as a binary-hierarchy problem over requests, identifying when a fixed global order is suboptimal. On BM25 retrieval traces from three BEIR corpora, the layout reduces prefill computation by 17–36% compared with production RAG ordering.

arXiv: [arXiv:2609.13692](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2609.13692)
chunks.about-research#4:
Rong He | 2026-09-10 | Preprint · Zenodo v0.10

Constructs stationary binary hidden Markov models with strictly positive transitions and emissions whose observations conceal the direction of time at any 2n − 4 sampling instants. Establishes a matching, sharp sample-complexity bound for detection.

Zenodo: [10.5281/zenodo.22684761](https://zenodo.org/records/22684761)
